transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen, Diego Marquez (Redwood); Priya Rao, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martins (Marigold)

[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alyssa, account exec at Redwood. Diego's with me — SE — and we wanted to kick off with how you're thinking about latency and capacity.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, thanks. I'm Priya, head of ML. We've got a few goals — low p95 for our short prompts and sustainable token/sec for bulk processing. We're also juggling compliance for customer data.
[00:34] Diego: Great. Can you share numbers? p95 expectations, concurrency, and what "short" looks like?
[00:45] Priya: For chat we want p95 under 350 ms for under 256 tokens ideally, and for streaming long-form (1k+ tokens) we'd accept up to 800–900 ms p95 but with stable token/sec. Concurrency wise: baseline 150 concurrent users, burst to 300 for 10–15 minutes during peak runs.
[01:10] Liam: Our traffic is spiky — logistics planning at end of day — and we need graceful degradation, not hard failures. Also, some workloads are large batch embedding runs — thousands of documents nightly.
[01:25] Alyssa: That's helpful. Quick clarification — when you say p95 for under 256 tokens, is that server-side end-to-end (request in to first token out) or full streaming tail?
[01:38] Sofia: End-to-end for first token is more valuable to us, because UI needs quick first reply. Streaming tail latency can be higher as long as token/sec remains steady.
[01:47] Diego: Understood. So we should target p95 first-token under 350 ms for short prompts, and sustainable token throughput for long sequences. A couple of things to call out: model family, whether you need deterministic outputs, and any private deployment constraints — those change the sizing.
[02:10] Priya: We're evaluating a mix of open and licensed models. For higher QA features we want a slightly bigger model but are open to quantized variants for cost. Data residency — some EU customers — so VPC or private deployment is on the table.
[02:28] Alyssa: Perfect. Hosted is quickest to launch; Dedicated gives reserved capacity and isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) handles strict residency and control. Tradeoffs: latency predictability vs ops overhead.
[02:40] Liam: For Dedicated, what latency guarantees or SLOs do you usually commit to?
[02:47] Diego: We have internal SLO examples for Dedicated with p95 latency targets tied to GPU class and batching policies. For example, on A800-class nodes with our continuous-batching optimizations, we've seen p95 ~220–400 ms for short prompts depending on model and sequence length. But we can tune kernels, quantization, and batching to balance cost.
[03:10] Priya: Could you share kernel/quantization tradeoffs? We worry about quality regressions with aggressive quant.
[03:18] Diego: Sure. We recommend starting with 8-bit quant on non-critical paths and running a small eval set to measure regressions. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles by workload. We'll include quality delta metrics in the benchmark template.
[03:34] Alyssa: Also want to check: do you need cross-region failover? You mentioned EU residency plus US ops.
[03:42] Sofia: Yes, EU data must stay in region for certain flows. We may route anonymized signals to US for analytics, but primary inference should be in EU.
[03:51] Diego: That maps well to our smart routing — policy can pin EU requests to EU Dedicated or Private nodes and fall back to compatible model variants in other regions only if policy allows. We'll document that in the ops checklist.
[04:06] Priya: On benchmarking — we need to know token/sec per GPU, aggregate token/sec across cluster, and p95 tail under representative load.
[04:16] Diego: Right. For planning, we usually ask for: representative prompt set, token length histogram, concurrency distribution, and target SLOs. We'll run an initial lightweight benchmark using our script and share results.
[04:28] Liam: Can you show an example of a benchmark run? What metrics do you collect?
[04:34] Diego: We collect p50/p90/p95 latencies for first token and full completion, tokens/sec per second, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rates. We'll add end-to-end wall time inc network.
[04:48] Alyssa: Quick question from procurement: what compliance docs can you share? SOC 2, ISO, data processing agreements, encryption details?
[04:57] Sofia: And we use HashiCorp Vault and our KMS, so key management integration is important.
[05:05] Alyssa: We can share SOC2 and our ISO attestation; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM in the on-prem package. We'll add the compliance contact to the deck.
[05:16] Priya: Good. Another requirement: fallback behavior during capacity pressure — we prefer automatic model variant fallback rather than queueing or 429s.
[05:26] Diego: We offer automatic fallback to smaller quantized or distilled variants with graceful substitution policies. For streaming workloads, we can also throttle token rate or lower sample size before rejecting.
[05:38] Liam: Do you support prefix/KV caching for multi-turn chat? That could save a lot of compute for our routing scenarios.
[05:44] Diego: Yes, Redwood's runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching. Note the transcript: sometimes the transcriber says K-V cash — apologies — but it's KV cache. That will reduce token compute on repeated context.
[05:58] Priya: About the burst to 300 concurrent, how do you size GPU pools? Is it request-based or token-based?
[06:06] Diego: We use a token/sec model combined with concurrency. For example, if each active stream averages 10 tokens/sec, 300 streams is ~3k tokens/sec; we then map to per-GPU token/sec capacity depending on model. We'll include model-specific numbers in the benchmark template.
[06:21] Alyssa: We're going to propose two pilot options: hosted with autoscale + guarded SLA for a month of traffic simulation, or a Dedicated pilot with reserved nodes to validate p95. Which would you prefer to start?
[06:33] Priya: Hosted pilot first to iterate rapidly. If we see stable SLOs, then Dedicated procurement. But we need to validate region residency during pilot.
[06:43] Sofia: And we want to run a long-form streaming workload for 24 hours to see token drift and tail behavior.
[06:50] Diego: Good. We'll provide a long-run test harness and suggest throttling knobs for steady-state testing.
[06:57] Liam: Any guidance for UI-level fallbacks — should we spec client-side token capping?
[07:05] Alyssa: We often advise client-side max tokens and progressive rendering; that reduces perceived latency even if backend slows.
[07:12] Priya: Let's talk numbers — do you have per-GPU token/sec baselines for common models?
[07:18] Diego: As a very rough starting point: for a Llama2-13B variant on A800, you might see 6k–10k tokens/sec single-GPU for generation when optimized; for 70B models it's lower, 1.5k–3k tokens/sec. Those are rough and depend on sequence length, KV caching, and quantization. We'll provide specific profiling.
[07:38] Priya: That helps. For our workload mix — 60% short chat, 30% long streaming, 10% batch embeddings — how would you approach capacity?
[07:48] Diego: We'll run a simulated mix in the benchmark. Usually you'd reserve capacity to cover p95 for short chat and allow batching/caching to absorb the long streaming. If bursts are short, burst capacity can be autoscaled or use dedicated reserved headroom.
[08:04] Sofia: For autoscale, what are typical cold-start delays when spinning new nodes?
[08:10] Diego: For Dedicated we pre-warm images; typical cold-start is a minute or two to allocate and warm model, but we advise using warm pools for critical paths to keep p95 stable.
[08:21] Alyssa: We'll map out a playbook: warm pool sizing, autoscale thresholds, and fallback policies.
[08:27] Priya: On metrics: we want token-level cost breakdowns by route and model. Can Redwood Console show token-level cost per route?
[08:35] Alyssa: Yes, Redwood Console can break down token cost, latency per-route, and per-token trace details. We can send a sample dashboard screenshot.
[08:43] Liam: About private deployment — if we go that route, how much ops effort to maintain kernels and runtime?
[08:50] Diego: Private includes a private control plane and an on-prem runner with automated updates. There is still an ops surface — patch management, HSM integration, network egress controls — but we provide an ops checklist and remote support options.
[09:04] Priya: We need evals to detect quality regressions from quant. Can you integrate our eval harness?
[09:11] Diego: Yes — we can run your eval set against each quant/profile and report delta metrics. Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles automatically but we'll validate with your ground truth.
[09:22] Sofia: What's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated on a per-token basis?
[09:27] Alyssa: It depends on committed capacity and burst patterns — typically Dedicated lowers unit cost with a commit, hosted is pay-as-you-go higher per-token but zero infra ops. We'll include pricing scenarios in the pilot quote.
[09:40] Priya: For the benchmark run, what do you need from us?
[09:43] Diego: Representative prompts, a token length histogram (counts per token bucket), concurrency trace for 24 hours, any special rules (like must-stay-in-EU), and a list of models you want profiled.
[09:55] Liam: We'll provide that. Also, we're using SAML SSO and SCIM — any friction?
[09:59] Alyssa: We support SAML and SCIM; sometimes the auto-import of groups needs a small mapping script but generally straightforward.
[10:07] Priya: Let's sketch the pilot timeline — we want initial hosted pilot for 2 weeks of simulated traffic then decision window.
[10:13] Alyssa: Reasonable. We'll prepare a hosted pilot plan: bench baseline in week 1, stress test and 24h streaming run in week 2, deliver report and next-step recommendation at the end.
[10:23] Diego: For the stress test, we'll push to your burst levels and measure p95 under tuned batching. We'll capture token/sec, p95 first token, and tail behavior.
[10:31] Sofia: On alerts, can Redwood Console emit SLO regression alerts tied to prompt sets?
[10:36] Diego: Yes, we can configure eval-linked alerts — if a prompt set's quality falls past threshold or latency SLOs exceed, it triggers alarms.
[10:44] Priya: Regarding failover: if EU Dedicated full, can we route to a smaller EU model in the same region as fallback rather than cross-region?
[10:52] Diego: Yes, policy can prefer same-region fallbacks to avoid data residency issues. We can chain compatible variants in the fallback stack.
[11:00] Alyssa: Quick pause — I want to note action item: Diego will provide the benchmark template and scripts.
[11:07] Diego: Noted. I'll put the scripts in the shared drive and include instructions.
[11:12] Priya: Also, please include a sample prompt list for long streaming to mimic our document summarization flows.
[11:18] Diego: Will do.
[11:20] Liam: A question about billing: do you support token-based reservations?
[11:24] Alyssa: Yes, Dedicated can be structured as committed tokens/hour or reserved GPUs; we can show modeled cost at different commit levels.
[11:32] Priya: Anything else on security — audit logs, access controls?
[11:36] Alyssa: We capture detailed audit logs and offer RBAC and SSO integrations. For Private, logs can remain in-custody per your retention policy.
[11:45] Sofia: Okay good — let's talk about risk: what are common failure modes in your production clusters?
[11:51] Diego: We've seen network egress saturation and NVMe stalls as primary causes; we mitigate with autoscaling, circuit breakers, and per-tenant isolation. For streaming tails, slow tail tokens can be from long history context — KV cache and chunking strategies help.
[12:10] Priya: That aligns with our ops teams suspicion.
[12:13] Alyssa: We're about halfway — any more deep technical dives we should schedule?
[12:18] Sofia: We want an on-prem ops deep dive with our infra team to go over KMS and firewall rules.
[12:24] Alyssa: We'll set that up for week of 2028-03-20.
[12:27] Diego: Also recommend a technical deep dive during the pilot to tweak batching.
[12:31] Priya: Agreed.
[12:33] Alyssa: Let's fast-forward to failure scenarios — token surge and graceful degradation example. Diego, can you sketch what happens?
[12:40] Diego: Sure. If surge exceeds reserved capacity, policy triggers fallbacks: 1) route to smaller model variant in-region, 2) reduce per-request token limit via a throttling policy, 3) if still saturated, shed non-critical routes. This keeps chat routes alive while background embedding jobs may be queued.
[12:59] Liam: We prefer embeddings be worker-queued rather than degrade chat.
[13:04] Diego: Policy supports route-level priorities so you can pin chat as high priority.
[13:10] Priya: For long streaming, can you limit token/sec per stream?
[13:14] Diego: Yes, token-rate limiting per connection is supported, we can do soft caps that nudge clients to back off.
[13:20] Alyssa: Any outstanding procurement items?
[13:23] Liam: We'll need a template MSA and DPA to start review.
[13:27] Alyssa: We'll include those in the pilot packet.
[13:31] Priya: About monitoring: can we get per-route p95 heatmaps and per-model token cost heatmaps?
[13:38] Diego: Yes, Redwood Console supports heatmaps and trace filters; we'll include sample configs.
[13:42] Sofia: A question about observability retention — if we keep high-res traces for 90 days, what's the cost?
[13:49] Alyssa: That's an add-on; we'll provide pricing options.
[13:53] Priya: One more thing — for the 24h streaming run, we'd like per-token latency distribution, not just p95.
[13:59] Diego: We'll capture full distribution and tail histograms and point to examples.
[14:05] Alyssa: Great. Let's summarize next steps and owners.
[14:08] Alyssa: 1) Alyssa — send pilot pricing and MSA/DPA by Friday (2028-03-17). 2) Diego — benchmark template and script by 2028-03-18. 3) Priya/Liam — send prompt set and token histograms by 2028-03-19. 4) Schedule on-prem ops deep dive week of 2028-03-20.
[14:30] Priya: Sounds good. Any last questions?
[14:34] Sofia: No, thanks. Appreciate the pragmatic plan.
[14:37] Alyssa: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[14:41] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-labels — speaker labels autogenerated; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Dedicayed" for Redwood Dedicated, "samel" for SAML). Please refer to the summary and action items above for canonical items.

End of transcript.
